A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD1 molecules are MHC class I-like molecules that bind and present lipid and glycolipid antigens to T cells.

the CD1 locus encods four genes, each of which is expressed on the cell surface and each of which is highly homologous to MHC class-I molecules, but which are distinct from MHC class-I and from each other.
CD1 molecules are MHC-like molecules, and CD1d is a fourth member of this family.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human CD1 locus is composed of at least five genes and that the CD1 proteins are more closely related to each other than to the MHC class I proteins.
CD1d is expressed in the thymus, spleen, and peripheral blood, but not on Langerhans cell lines.
CD1 is a highly polymorphic molecule that is encoded by a gene complex on chromosome 1.
